title: Time-lapse maths
summary: Interval, number of shots and how long to wait.

blocks.text: Each photo becomes one frame of the video. Two sums plan any time-lapse:

items: **Shots = clip length × frame rate.** A 10 s clip at 30 fps needs 300 shots.
**Shooting time = shots × interval.** 300 shots every 3 s takes 15 minutes.
**Lock everything:** manual exposure, white balance and focus, or the video flickers and shifts colour.
The interval must be longer than the shutter plus a second or two to save the shot.
Smoother motion: a shutter of about half the interval blurs movement slightly. An ND filter helps in daylight.
Check battery and card space first. Hundreds of RAW files fill a card fast.
